To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of pairing stimuli with food are mediated by the effects of the same stimuli upon the occurrence of prepecking behavior.

the approach toward the lighted key is sensitive to its consequences, that the peck at that key occurs when a food-reinforced approach toward the key occurs in the presence of a stimulus previously paired with food, and that the peck is sensitive to its own consequences.
the effects of pairing the keylight and food are mediated by the effects of adventitious food reinforcements of the approach toward and the pecking at the key.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of reinforcement upon prepecking behavior in the autoshape procedure.
the effects of the autoshaping procedure upon the acquisition of the peck at a keylight.
the role of the approach response in the acquisition of the key peck in the autoshape experiment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of reinforcement upon autoshaped pecking in pigeons are due to the effects of the stimuli present during the approach to the key.
autoshaping is the product of a complex interaction of several variables.

autoshaped pecking is not determined by pairing a stimulus with food, but rather by a combination of the pairing of a stimulus with food and the adventitious reinforcement of the approach toward and peck at the stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
autoshaped key pecks occur when a stimulus is presented that has been previously paired with food and when a response occurs that has been reinforced by food in the presence of that stimulus.

the autoshaping phenomenon is not a simple one, and that it is necessary to consider the effects of both stimulus-reinforcer relations and response-reinforcement relations upon the occurrence of the orienting, approach, and peck responses.
peck acquisition is determined by the interaction of the stimulus-reinforcer effect of the light and the response-reinforcer effect that the approach toward the light has upon the peck.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the autoshaping procedure is a very powerful procedure for producing key pecking, but that this procedure is also a confounding procedure in that it confounds the effects upon key pecking of stimulus-reinforcement and response-reinforcement variables.
the pecking behavior of the pigeon is a complex behavior that is determined by multiple antecedent variables.

the autoshaping phenomenon is not a single effect, but rather is composed of several different effects, each of which may be studied separately. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
